newsitem.title: USA: U.S regulator proposes rule for thrift conversions.
newsitem.headline: U.S regulator proposes rule for thrift conversions.

text.p: Office of Thrift Supervision Wednesday proposed a rule to make it easier for credit unions to convert to mutual savings associations.
Federal courts imposed strict membership limits on federally chartered credit unions last year, although the Supreme Court has said it will hear an appeal next term.

"The proposed rule change is in keeping with OTS's belief that depository institutions should be free to operate under whatever charter they deem best suits their business needs, consistent with safety and soundness," OTS director Nicholas Retsinas said in a statement.
The agency currently allows stock depository institutions and state-chartered mutual savings banks and savings and loans to convert directly to federal mutual savings associations.
However, other mutual institutions such as credit unions must go through several steps to make the same change, the agency said.
That can involve obtaining several different regulatory approvals, which "is more burdensome," the agency said.
The proposed rule was published in the Federal Register on Wednesday. Comments will be accepted for 60 days, OTS said.
